Name: Katie Cornine
Badge: Teacher as Researcher: Cultivating Literacy Routines
Looking back on this inquiry cycle, what did you learn about your teaching and your students that you might not have noticed otherwise? How did engaging in this teacher-research process shape or shift your thinking about your classroom practice?:

They Say/I Say During this activity, I noticed different foundational skills that need to be touched on during future meetings with my small title reading group. It was low-stakes writing, so I think that students wrote more than they would with just a writing prompt. The thing I loved about this activity was that my ELLs had a great discussion about what the text was saying. We did a lot of discussion before I had them write. I feel like this activity shaped my teaching because I plan to use my writing activities in my small reading groups.

Share one artifact or anecdote from trying out your chosen strategy (e.g., a piece of student work, notes from your Writer’s Notebook, a classroom snapshot, or a brief story from the experience).:
What new questions or next steps are you leaving this module with? How might you continue to explore or build on this inquiry in your future teaching?:

How can I incorporate this activity into all of my small reading groups? How can I modify this activity to use with all my students in grades K-8? How can I change the structure of my small reading groups to fit in not only this writing activity, but also the activities that were used in all of the modules? I plan to collaborate with my fellow teachers that particpated in this course and see how they are using these activities in their classroom.
